full_judgment:
2. In Writ Petition No, 9435 of 2012 the Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the Order Nos.22 and 23 dated 22-3-2012 and ex-parte judgment and decree dated 22-3-2012 (decree signed on 25-3-2012) passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka in Artha Rin Suit No. 276 of 2010 ignoring an application for withdrawal of the suit from ex-parte hearing in contravention of the provisions of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 should not be Declared to have, been passed without lawful authority and are of no legal effect and/or such other or further order, or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. In Writ Petition No. 9436 of 2012 the Rule Nisi was issued calling upon. the respondents to show cause as to why the Order Nos. 22 and 23 dated 22-3-2012 and ex-parte judgment and decree dated 22-3-2012 (decree signed on 25-3-2012) passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka in Artha Rin Suit No.277 of 2010 ignoring an application for withdrawal of the suit from ex-parte hearing in contravention of the provisions of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and are of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 5. The petitioners as defendants appeared in both the suits on 7-2-2010 and prayed for time to file written statement which was allowed by the court and subsequently filed an application in both the suits under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for rejection of the plaints in both the suits. The respondent No.1 court upon contested hearing rejected the said application vide order No. 21 dated 4-3-2012. Thereafter the, petitioners in both the suits filed an application on 22-3-2012 praying for withdrawal of the suits from the list of ex-parte hearing and prayed for time to submit written statements on behalf of the petitioners but the respondent No.1 after hearing rejected the application 'and proceeded' with ex-parte hearing and decreed the suit ex-parte by order No. 23 dated 22-3-2012. Hence the petitioners.moved this court under Article 102 of the Constitution challenging the ex-parte decree and obtained the present rule. 

 8. On 6-6-2011 the petitioner filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with section 57 orthe Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 with a fresh vokalatnama and filed another application praying for withdrawal of the suit from ex-parte hearing list and for hearing the application for rejection of plaint. The court heard the application for withdrawal of suit from ex-parte hearing and rejected the assigning the reasons and fixed 29-6-2011 for hearing application under Order VII, rule 11, CPC and ex- parte hearing. On that day the respondent No. 2 filed written objection against the application under Order VII, rule 11, CPC, The court fixed 6-7-2011 for hearing application for rejection of plaint and ex-parte hearing. On 6-7-2011 the petitioner filed time petition which was allowed and fixed 19-7-2011 for application hearing on 19-7-2011 the application was not heard as the court was busy with other cases. Thereafter, 14-8-2011 was fixed for hearing the application and on that date the application was heard and fixed on 4-9-2011 for order. Subsequently, the date of order got deferred several times on the ground of the engagement of the court with other matters. Finally, the case was fixed for order on 4-3-2012 and the Court passed the order and rejected the application for rejection of the plaint on' the ground stated therein and fixed 22-3-2012 for ex- parte hearing. On 22-3-12 the petitioners again filed an application praying for withdrawal of the suit from ex-parte list and allow them to file written statements. The court upon hearing rejected the application assigning reasons vide order No, 22 dated 22-3-2012. After rejection of the application for time the petitioners neither took any step nor filed hazira or written statements but remained absent. The petitioner having thus being failed to file written statements and found to have been absent on the date when the case was called for hearing the court proceeded with the ex parte hearing and decreed the suit ex-parte vide order No. 23 dated 22-3-2012. Subsequently, the respondent No.2 filed Artha Jari Case No. 157 of 2012 on 22-7-2012 for execution of the decree and notices under section 30 of the Ain duly served upon the petitioners but they did not take any steps for payment of the decretal amount. Consequently, the court issued warrants of arrest against the petitioners on 4-10-2012, but the petitioners somehow managed to evade arrest. 

 10. Mr M Sayed Ahmed with Mr Imtiaz Farooq, the learned Advocates appearing for the petitioners, referring to order sheets submit that the impugned orders of the respondent No.1 court are absolutely void, vitiated by malafide, and in excess of jurisdiction, and contrary to the provisions of law. The learned Advocates put stress on order No.5 dated 16-1-2011 wherein the court treated service of summons, upon the petitioners and fixed the suit on 7-2-2011 for ex-parte hearing and order Nos. 22 and 23 dated 22-3-2012 on which date the suit was decreed ex-parte upon rejection of the prayer of the petitioners to withdraw the case from ex-parte list, thereby, enabling them to file written statements. They further submit that fixing of date for ex-parte hearing by the court vide order No.5 dated 16-1-2011 is malafide and contrary to the provisions of law as the Ain does not provide any provision for ex-parte hearing except under circumstances and situation arising under sections 10 and 19 of the Ain, these being the failure of the defendants to file written statements under section 10 of the Ain or the defendants remaining absent on the date fixed for hearing or found to be absent on call when a case is taken up for hearing. They further submit that the court violated the provisions of law firstly in fixing the suit for ex-parte hearing vide order No.5 dated 16-1-2011 and secondly in proceeding with the ex-parte hearing by rejecting the application of the petitioners to withdraw the suit from ex-parte hearing list and to file written statements. As per interpretation given by the learned Advocates for the petitioners, section 19(1) of the Ain allows ex-parte hearing under two situations, e.g, (i) absence of the defendants on the date fixed for hearing of the suit, and (ii) the defendant's being found absent when the case is actually taken up for hearing. According to them the court cannot fix the suit for ex-parte hearing after service of notice without fixing a date for filing written statements under section 10 of the Ain and, as such, fixing of the suit for ex-parte hearing is without jurisdiction and the decree passed ex-parte is also without jurisdiction and in violation of the provisions of law. 

 11. On the other hand, Mr Ruhul Ameen, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.2 submits that the court committed no illegality and violated no provisions of law as the court allowed time to the petitioners under section 10 of the Act and provided sufficient opportunity to file written statements but the petitioners failed to file written statements within the time fixed by law as well as allowed by the court. He also submits that after service of summons upon the petitioners they did not appear on the date fixed on 16-1-2011 as such, in the absence of defendants the court had no alternative but to fix the suit for ex-parte hearing on 7-2-2011. Thereafter, on the date fixed for ex-parte hearing the defendants appeared in the suit and on the prayer of the petitioners the respondent No.1 court has withdrawn the suit from ex-parte list and allowed them to file written statements but the petitioners failed to file written statements even within the extended period as prescribed by law. Accordingly, repeated failures of the petitioners in filing written statements has compelled the court to fix the suit for ex-parte hearing again on 22-5-2011. Indeed, from 6-6- 2011 to 22-3-2012, the suit was fixed in the list of ex-parte hearing but the petitioners within this period also utterly failed to file written statements and, as such, the court had no alternative other than to proceed with ex-parte hearing. As such the court has committed no illegality in passing the impugned decrees. Mr Ameen further submits that there being specific remedy in the statute for filing appeal against the judgments and decrees under section 41 and provision also for filing application for setting-aside the ex-parte decree, in the present case the petitioners having not availed of the aforesaid remedies cannot now seek redress through these writ petitions. He further submits that the respondent No.2 after obtaining ex-parte decree filed Artha Jari Case for execution of the decree in which warrants of arrest have already issued against the petitioners. In the circumstances, he prays for discharging the rule. 

 13. In view of the submissions made by the learned Advocates for the parties firstly, we are to see whether the court in passing the ex-parte decree exceeded its jurisdiction or acted contrary to the provisions of law and whether the decision of the court has vitiated by malafide. Secondly, it is to be examined whether the petitioners can seek any relief under writ jurisdiction against the ex-parte decrees where there are specific provisions in the Ain to challenge the decrees so passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. 

 19. Now, we are to see whether the defendant can invoke provisions of section 19(2), of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain in the event of ex-parte decree passed under section 10(1) of the Ain for the failure of the defendant to file written statements. We find that clearly there are no provisions in section 10 of the Ain for filing applications against the ex-parte judgments and decrees of the Artha Rin Adalat similar to the provisions contained in section 19(2) of the Ain. Given that secnario, it is this Court's considered view that it was open to the defendant in the facts and circumstances to explore possible avenues of redress otherwise available under the Ain. Here, while the appeal provisions of section 41 come immediately to mind, in addition, a reading of section 26 of the Act serves to provide an indication of invoking relevant provisions of the Code. However, beyond this, we are unable presently to explore further that latter scenario of any avenue of redress under the Code given that such point, was not raised or submitted upon at any length by any party to the present Writ Petitions. 

 21. The learned Advocates for the petitioners further submit that the present writ petitions are maintainable because the impugned judgments and decrees passed by the respondent No.1, court are vitiated by malafide and the court acted in excess of jurisdiction, and contrary to the provisions of law tantamount to malice in law. In support of their submissions they referred to the case of Mir Motiur Rahman Zihadi vs Artha Rin Adalat, Tangail reported in 15 BLT(AD) 267 and an unreported judgment passed by another Bench of this Division in the case of Delwar Hossain Chowdhury vs Joint District Judge, Sylhet, in Writ Petition No, 7347 of 2010, the fact of which, however, are totally different in substance from the present case. '.; 

 22. In reply to the aforesaid submissions the learned Advocate for the respondent No.2 submitted that the present petitions are not maintainable as there being special provision for appeal in the Artha Rin Adalat Ain against the judgment and decree under section 41 of the Ain upon payment of 50% of the decretal money and for filing an application for setting-aside; the ex-parte decree. In this connection he referred to a catena of cases Zahirul Islam vs NBL reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191, BADC vs Artha Rin Adalat reported in 59 DLR (AD) 6 and Gazi M Towfic vs Agrani Bank reported in 54 DLR (AD) 6. 

 23. In the aforesaid cases the petitioners moved the High Court Division under Article 102of the Constitution challenging the judgments and decrees of the Artha Rin Adalat on various grounds including malafide and violations of law and the fact of the judgments being passed in excess of jurisdiction. The Appellate Division held that, "Since special provision for appeal has been made against the judgment and decree passed by Artha Rin Adalat no application under Article 102 lies against such judgment and decree" reference 54 DLR (AD) 6. 

 25. In view of the decisions quoted and observations made above we are led to the irresistible conclusion that there being specific remedy in the statute for filing appeal or application as observed above against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, in the present case the defendant not availing of the aforesaid remedy cannot now in lieu of that process now maintain the writ petitions and, as such, the Rules are liable to be discharged.
